description.value: A study of healthy adults in dating relationships examining whether LPFC neural activity during partner and stranger facial-expression viewing predicts mood and behavior after interpersonal conflict.

spans.text: We used functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) along with behavioral tasks and a daily diary study to test whether LPFC neural response to a laboratory-based affective challenge would predict regulation of mood and behavior in response to a real-life affective challenge—an interpersonal conflict with a partner.

value: We predicted that although everyone would experience an increase in negative mood on the day of interpersonal conflict, recovery from this negative event by the following day would depend on LPFC function.
